section_summary: This section documents Japanese bank balances, dollar bonds, silver purchases, and the effects of restrictions on credit and Japanese funds in 1941. Much of it concerns Japanese financing of minerals and other goods in South America, including bank credits, shipments of gold, and Argentine hides. It ends with correspondence about scrap rubber exports and private holders of Japanese bonds.

subfiles.title: Japanese balances at Chase National Bank, July 18
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese account balances and a sharp weekly decline in Yokohama Specie Bank funds.
subfiles.summary: FBI figures place Japanese accounts at $3,840,113 on July 18.

subfiles.title: Japanese cash withdrawals from New York banks
subfiles.about: Relays Cameron’s report of Japanese withdrawals and inquiries about further cash withdrawals.
subfiles.summary: Reports large withdrawals and a request for additional $1,000 bills.

subfiles.title: Payee of Yokohama Specie Bank withdrawal
subfiles.about: Identifies the payee of a Chase National Bank cash withdrawal as a Yokohama Specie Bank employee.
subfiles.summary: The check was reportedly payable to J. Malligan.

subfiles.title: Further Yokohama Specie Bank cash withdrawal
subfiles.about: Reports a further cash withdrawal by Malligan for the Yokohama Specie Bank.
subfiles.summary: The OCR is damaged, but records another substantial withdrawal and a preceding withdrawal.

subfiles.title: Transfer notation for file 894.51/734
subfiles.about: Records transfer of a document to another decimal file.
subfiles.summary: Transferred to file 894.506.

subfiles.title: Routing note on Japanese silver financing
subfiles.about: Recommends replying to Emerson in line with Acheson’s position.
subfiles.summary: Carr suggests EA reply and return the file to A-A, avoiding further delay.

subfiles.title: Acheson routing annotation
subfiles.about: Records a brief handwritten concurrence and suggestion on the silver financing matter.
subfiles.summary: The annotation is partly illegible.

subfiles.title: Luthringer memorandum on Japanese silver purchases
subfiles.about: Distinguishes purchasing Japanese silver from extending credit to finance payment at the dock.
subfiles.summary: Luthringer proposes expressing disapproval of borrowing against the silver under the Department’s established stance on credit to Japan.

subfiles.title: Assistant Secretary’s routing annotation
subfiles.about: Requests advice or a draft on the attached silver financing matter.
subfiles.summary: Handwritten text is largely illegible.

subfiles.title: Conversation with Guy Emerson on Baker and Company silver imports
subfiles.about: Records Bankers Trust’s inquiry about loans enabling Baker and Company to pay for Japanese silver on arrival.
subfiles.summary: Emerson says the imports run to millions of dollars annually and the loans effectively finance the Japanese silver market. Bell advises consulting Acheson before another loan.

subfiles.title: Reply to Bankers Trust on Japanese silver financing
subfiles.about: States the Department’s position on Japanese silver purchases and credit to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Department has no comment on the purchases but does not favor extending credit to Japan.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on Japanese fire insurers
subfiles.from: State Department Adviser on International Economic Affairs
subfiles.about: Points to a memorandum on two Japanese insurers ending U.S. fire insurance business.
subfiles.summary: References file 894.506/11 and retained funds for creditors.

subfiles.title: Japanese balances at Chase National Bank, July 11
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese bank balances and Mitsui debt secured by collateral.
subfiles.summary: The accounts total $8,858,495; Yokohama Specie Bank holds $7,924,171.

subfiles.title: Japanese deposits at Chase National Bank, July 3
subfiles.about: Lists gross and net Japanese deposits after commitments.
subfiles.summary: The reported net total is $7,304,158.

subfiles.title: Cravens forwards constituent’s Japanese bond inquiry
subfiles.about: Requests guidance for a constituent holding Japanese guaranteed bonds.
subfiles.summary: Cravens encloses Acruman’s letter and seeks an answer to pass along.

subfiles.title: Acruman inquiry about Japanese dollar bonds
subfiles.about: Asks how frozen Japanese funds affect interest and principal payments on his bonds.
subfiles.summary: He holds Oriental Development Company and City of Tokyo dollar bonds.

subfiles.title: Hull reply on Japanese bond payments
subfiles.about: Directs Acruman to paying agents and notes Treasury jurisdiction over restricted payments.
subfiles.summary: Japanese securities payments fall under the amended executive order governing foreign exchange and foreign property.

subfiles.title: Navy reports on Japanese economic conditions
subfiles.about: Forwards Navy Department letters on Japan’s economic conditions.
subfiles.summary: Confidential copies of July 11 and July 14 Navy letters are enclosed.

subfiles.title: Credits for mineral purchases in South America
subfiles.about: Transmits Yokohama Specie Bank credits for vanadium, antimony, copper and lead purchases.
subfiles.summary: Confidential bank telegrams specify beneficiaries, amounts, shipping routes and payment terms for mineral purchases in Peru, Bolivia, Chile and other west coast locations.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on Masatsune Ogura
subfiles.about: References a report on Ogura’s appointment to strengthen Japan’s cabinet.
subfiles.summary: Points to a Justice Department letter in file 894.002/490.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on Japanese currency for commodity purchases
subfiles.about: References a report that Japanese purchasers would receive currency for current commodity purchases.
subfiles.summary: Points to Bangkok telegram 438 in file 792.94/142.

subfiles.title: Additional mineral purchase credits
subfiles.about: Supplies further Japanese bank credits for mineral transactions in Bolivia and Chile.
subfiles.summary: Enclosed messages from the Bank of Taiwan and Yokohama Specie Bank cover copper and antimony shipments, revised beneficiaries, and additional Kobe credits.

subfiles.title: Finletter query on warning Argentina
subfiles.about: Seeks agreement on Feis’s proposal to cable the embassy in Argentina.
subfiles.summary: Finletter asks whether Bonsal agrees and who should draft the cable.

subfiles.title: Feis proposal to approach Argentine authorities
subfiles.about: Suggests directing the embassy to raise the reported Japanese transaction with Argentina.
subfiles.summary: Feis expects the approach itself to signal U.S. interest.

subfiles.title: British report on Japanese financing of Argentine hides
subfiles.about: Reports a secret Japanese effort to borrow German peso funds for Argentine hides.
subfiles.summary: The letter also describes proposed payment in goods and a nitrate transaction involving payment in Rio de Janeiro.

subfiles.title: Instruction to investigate Japanese hide financing
subfiles.about: Directs confidential discussion with Argentine authorities of reported Japanese borrowing.
subfiles.summary: The alleged German loan would provide peso funds worth seven million yen for hides.

subfiles.title: Further Yokohama Specie Bank mineral credits
subfiles.about: Forwards two additional Japanese mineral credit telegrams.
subfiles.summary: Credits cover molybdenite concentrate and lead ore shipped from Peru to Japan.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on Thai credit to Japan
subfiles.about: References talks about further credit from Thai banks to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Points to telegram 1508 in another file.

subfiles.title: Buenos Aires reply on Argentine hide financing
subfiles.about: Reports Argentine inquiries and recent Japanese shipments of hides.
subfiles.summary: Argentine contacts knew of no German arrangement; a yen draft reportedly resolved financing for one shipment.

subfiles.title: File copy of instruction on Argentine hides
subfiles.about: Repeats the Department’s instruction to discuss reported Japanese borrowing confidentially.
subfiles.summary: A separate file copy of telegram 681.

subfiles.title: Japanese gold landed in Peru
subfiles.about: Reports gold brought from Japan for cotton and wool purchases.
subfiles.summary: The Noto Maru landed 263 kilograms of gold at Callao after Peru declined yen exchange.

subfiles.title: British report on Japanese credits and yen in Peru
subfiles.about: Shares British information on Japanese purchase credits and a possible local market for yen.
subfiles.summary: The report describes $1 million for purchases in Peru, Chile and Bolivia, mainly Peruvian cotton.

subfiles.title: Argentine hide payment despatch
subfiles.about: Forwards a bank memorandum on how Japanese hide shipments were paid for.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum reportedly confirms Central Bank yen purchases and describes hides awaiting further shipment.

subfiles.title: Bank memorandum on Japanese hide shipments
subfiles.from: Assistant manager, First National Bank of Boston, Buenos Aires
subfiles.about: Details the Argentine hide trade with Japan and the financing disruption caused by frozen Japanese balances.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum names participating firms and shippers, estimates volumes, and describes a Central Bank yen transaction that enabled shipment. It also reports hides awaiting another vessel and speculates about German involvement.

subfiles.title: Central Bank account of hide payments
subfiles.about: Reports a Central Bank official’s correction to the earlier account of Japanese hide financing.
subfiles.summary: Grumbach says most pesos came from the compensation account; dollars held elsewhere in South America contributed negligibly.

subfiles.title: Gold aboard Toa Maru
subfiles.about: Reports 73 cases of gold landed in Buenos Aires for Argentine purchases.
subfiles.summary: Early estimates put its value above $5 million, possibly $10 million.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Toa Maru gold telegram
subfiles.about: Restates the initial report on gold carried by Toa Maru.
subfiles.summary: The paraphrase repeats uncertain $5 million and $10 million estimates.

subfiles.title: Revised estimate of Toa Maru gold
subfiles.about: Reports the manifest weight of gold aboard Toa Maru.
subfiles.summary: At 2,676 kilograms gross, its estimated value falls to about $3 million if pure.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of revised gold telegram
subfiles.about: Restates the revised Toa Maru gold estimate.
subfiles.summary: The paraphrase notes uncertainty about any gold omitted from the manifest.

subfiles.title: Gold telegrams forwarded to Treasury
subfiles.about: Transmits paraphrases of Buenos Aires telegrams about Japanese gold imports.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the October 17 and 18 reports.

subfiles.title: Japanese wool and vanadium credits in Peru
subfiles.about: Reports credits for alpaca wool, greasy wool and vanadium ash purchases.
subfiles.summary: One credit names T. Koike and a Peruvian wool seller; Yokohama Specie Bank cables specify two further letters of credit. The bank source is identified confidentially as Banco Italiano.

subfiles.title: Toa Maru gold valuation and cargo
subfiles.about: Revises the gold valuation and describes arrangements for Argentine goods carried by Toa Maru.
subfiles.summary: The gold was officially valued at about $1.75 million, though possibly worth more. The embassy reports direct Central Bank dealings with Yokohama Specie Bank and encloses a cargo list.

subfiles.title: Proposed Toa Maru cargo list
subfiles.about: Lists proposed cargo, exporters and destinations for Toa Maru’s departure.
subfiles.summary: Includes hides, wool, linseed, minerals and other goods.

subfiles.title: British report on Argentine scrap rubber
subfiles.about: Reports a credit for scrap rubber destined for Japan and British concern over the trade.
subfiles.summary: A $4,500 credit reportedly covers 60 tons; Britain is investigating and considering its rubber export licences.

subfiles.title: Instruction on Argentine scrap rubber exports
subfiles.about: Authorizes efforts to stop Argentine scrap rubber shipments to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The embassy may approach Argentine authorities and say the Rubber Reserve Corporation is prepared to negotiate a purchase.

subfiles.title: File docket 894.51/757
subfiles.about: Marks the filing of material under decimal number 894.51/757.
subfiles.summary: Contains only the file number and initials.

subfiles.title: British Admiralty report on gold at Callao
subfiles.about: Reports gold brought by Azuma Maru for Japanese merchant vessels.
subfiles.summary: The reported value is £150,000.

subfiles.title: Final Toa Maru cargo report
subfiles.about: Corrects the earlier Toa Maru cargo account using the published final manifest.
subfiles.summary: The ship carried 44,736 hides and 802 tons of quebracho extract. Wolframite and scheelite were removed following representations by Thomas J. Williams.

subfiles.title: Published final Toa Maru manifest
subfiles.about: Lists final cargo, shippers, consignees, quantities and destinations.
subfiles.summary: The translated manifest covers cargo bound for Yokohama, Kobe and Osaka.

subfiles.title: British report on Toa Maru bullion
subfiles.about: Reports a belief that Toa Maru unloaded bullion in Argentina and retained more for Brazil.
subfiles.summary: The figures reported are $3 million and $2 million respectively.

subfiles.title: Bank of Taiwan credit for Peruvian copper ore
subfiles.about: Transmits a confidential Bank of Taiwan credit for copper ore shipped from Peru to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The November 6 cable opens a ¥99,504 credit for roughly 450 tons from Mollendo. Banco Italiano requests restricted government use of the information.

subfiles.title: State Department forwards Peru credit report to Treasury
subfiles.about: Forwards the Lima despatch and requests guidance on a reply.
subfiles.summary: Encloses despatch 2147 on Japanese financial operations in Peru.

subfiles.title: Dent forwards Marris letter
subfiles.about: Forwards Marris’s letter about Japanese gold shipments.
subfiles.summary: Dent sends a copy of the October 27 letter.

subfiles.title: British summary of Japanese gold shipments
subfiles.about: Summarizes reports of Japanese gold arriving in South America.
subfiles.summary: The letter lists reported cargoes on Azuma Maru, Toa Maru, Terukawa Maru and Noto Maru. It says gold in Argentina would be exchanged for pesos used to buy Argentine goods.

subfiles.title: Gold shipment circular forwarded to Treasury
subfiles.about: Forwards a circular requesting reports on Japanese gold shipments.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the November 14 circular to missions in Central and South America.

subfiles.title: Circular inquiry on Japanese gold shipments
subfiles.to: Diplomatic missions in Central and South America
subfiles.about: Requests immediate reporting of Japanese gold shipments and their purpose.
subfiles.summary: Missions should distinguish payment for delivered goods from funds for future purchases.

subfiles.title: Japanese applications for credits through Bank of Brazil
subfiles.about: Records Donnelly’s report of Japanese requests for South American strategic material credits.
subfiles.summary: Thirty-two applications total $1.4 million. Donnelly urged the Bank of Brazil to refuse them; its exchange director sought a legal basis under U.S. freezing rules.

subfiles.title: Division routing annotation
subfiles.about: Contains a largely illegible Division of the American Republics annotation.
subfiles.summary: No substantive text can be read reliably.

subfiles.title: Buenos Aires reply on scrap rubber
subfiles.about: Reports approaches to Argentina about scrap rubber exports to Japan.
subfiles.summary: About 200 tons had been sold in 1941, but further shipments seemed unlikely. Argentine authorities were told of a possible Rubber Reserve Corporation purchase.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on funds transfers to Japan
subfiles.about: References assurances that no funds would be transferred to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Points to telegram 241 in the frozen credits file.

subfiles.title: Treasury acknowledgment of Lima despatch
subfiles.from: Treasury Department, Administrative Assistant to the Secretary
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the forwarded report on Japanese financial operations in Peru.
subfiles.summary: Treasury promises consideration and a later response.

subfiles.title: Treasury forwards Owen bond inquiry
subfiles.about: Refers J. Bailey Owen’s Japanese bond inquiry to State.
subfiles.summary: Pehle encloses Owen’s letter and says Owen was notified.

subfiles.title: Owen inquiry about Imperial Japanese Government bonds
subfiles.about: Asks whether seized Japanese funds could repay his Imperial Japanese Government bonds.
subfiles.summary: Owen fears losing his $5,000 investment after war begins.
